newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela makes 1996's biggest gains on IFC index.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela makes 1996's biggest gains on IFC index.

text.p: Venezuela made the biggest gains on the International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities for 1996, showing returns of more than 100 percent over the year.
By the start of the last trading day of 1996, Latin America had scored the biggest advances of the three emerging market regions, with Venezuela clocking up a return of 114.8 percent.

Venezuela, which embarked on a tough IMF-backed reform programme in April, came in well ahead of its nearest rival Hungary, which scored 98.3 percent over the year, and Zimbabwe, which scored 71.6 percent.
Thailand was the index's biggest loser. Hit by economic woes and a political crisis that culminated in snap elections in November, it shed 41.1 percent over the year.
Korea was the second poorest performer, shedding 38.6 percent, while South Africa lost 19.3 percent.
As a region, Latin America gained 13.8 percent against Asia's 7.8 percent. Europe, the Middle East and Africa as a group, however, lost 5.5 percent over the year up to and including 30 December 1996.

The IFC's composite investable index measures returns in dollar terms on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market nations and is used by investors to benchmark portfolio performance.
The index gained 6.4 percent over the year. Figures for 1995 were not immediately available.
Meanwhile, the JP Morgan composite Emerging Market Bond Index, updated after Monday's close of trade, was up nearly 40 percent at 143.73 over the year to December 30.
Russia was the year's biggest gainer, up a spectacular 113.09 percent. South Africa was the year's worst performer, climbing only 8.63 percent over the same period.
